extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (educational institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX compliance for educational recipients
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and definitions from the Department of Education's Title IX final rule governing nondiscrimination, grievance procedures, coordinator designation, training, recordkeeping, pregnancy accommodations, and institutional responses to sex discrimination for recipients of Federal financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental status
rubrics_metrics.description: Parental status, as used in §§ 106.21(c)(2)(i), 106.37(a)(3), 106.40(a), and 106.57(a)(1), means the status of a person who, with respect to another person who is under the age of 18 or who is 18 or older but is incapable of self-care because of a physical or mental disability, is: (1) A biological parent; (2) An adoptive parent; (3) A foster parent; (4) A stepparent; (5) A legal custodian or guardian; (6) In loco parentis with respect to such a person; or (7) Actively seeking legal custody, guardianship, visitation, or adoption of such a person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in multiple provisions (e.g., admissions, pregnancy-related protections) to identify who qualifies as a 'parent' for purposes of Title IX protections and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party
rubrics_metrics.description: Party means a complainant or respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer retaliation means retaliation by a student against another student.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institution means an institution of graduate higher education, an institution of undergraduate higher education, an institution of professional education, or an institution of vocational education that serves postsecondary school students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy or related conditions (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pregnancy or related conditions means: (1) Pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, or lactation; (2) Medical conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, or lactation; or (3) Recovery from pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, lactation, or related medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline definitional standard used across admissions, program access, and accommodations provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program or activity / program (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program or activity and program means all of the operations of—(1)(i) A department, agency, special purpose district, or other instrumentality of a State or local government; or (ii) The entity of a State or local government that distributes such assistance and each such department or agency (and each other State or local government entity) to which the assistance is extended... (2)(i) A college, university, or other postsecondary institution, or a public system of higher education; or (ii) A local educational agency...; (3) Entire corporation/partnership/private organization or entire sole proprietorship in specified circumstances; or (4) Any other entity established by two or more of the entities described above, any part of which is extended Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of entities and operations covered by Title IX obligations; includes specific coverage rules for government entities, educational systems, healthcare/social-service organizations, and multi-entity arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient means any State or political subdivision thereof, or any instrumentality of a State or political subdivision thereof, any public or private agency, institution, or organization, or other entity, or any person, to whom Federal financial assistance is extended directly or through another recipient and which operates an education program or activity which receives such assistance, including any subunit, successor, assignee, or transferee thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies who is legally bound by the Part's requirements — broadly covers public and private entities that receive Federal financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant (in investigations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant means related to the allegations of sex discrimination under investigation as part of the grievance procedures under § 106.45, and if applicable § 106.46. Questions are relevant when they seek evidence that may aid in showing whether the alleged sex discrimination occurred, and evidence is relevant when it may aid a decisionmaker in determining whether the alleged sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the evidentiary relevance test for questions and evidence in grievance procedures and hearings; ties relevance to the ability to aid factfinding on whether sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies means measures provided, as appropriate, to a complainant or any other person the recipient identifies as having had their equal access to the recipient's education program or activity limited or denied by sex discrimination. These measures are provided to restore or preserve that person's access to the recipient's education program or activity after a recipient determines that sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that remedies are individualized measures to restore equal access following a determination of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent means a person who is alleged to have violated the recipient's prohibition on sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retaliation means intimidation, threats, coercion, or discrimination against any person by the recipient, a student, or an employee or other person authorized by the recipient to provide aid, benefit, or service under the recipient's education program or activity, for the purpose of interfering with any right or privilege secured by Title IX or this part, or because the person has reported information, made a complaint, testified, assisted, or participated or refused to participate in any manner in an investigation, proceeding, or hearing under this part... Nothing in this definition or this part precludes a recipient from requiring an employee or other person authorized by a recipient to provide aid, benefit, or service under the recipient's education program or activity to participate as a witness in, or otherwise assist with, an investigation, proceeding, or hearing under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers retaliation by institutions, employees, or students and clarifies recipients may require certain employees or authorized persons to assist in investigations despite retaliation protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing authority means that component of the Department delegated authority by the Secretary to appoint, and to review the decisions of, administrative law judges in cases arising under this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary school (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary school means secondary school as defined by section 8101 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965... and an institution of vocational education that serves secondary school students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex-based harassment (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex-based harassment prohibited by this part is a form of sex discrimination and means sexual harassment and other harassment on the basis of sex, including on the bases described in § 106.10, that is: (1) Quid pro quo harassment; (2) Hostile environment harassment; or (3) Specific offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This umbrella definition organizes prohibited conduct into three categories (quid pro quo; hostile environment; specific offenses) each with its own elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quid pro quo harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee, agent, or other person authorized by the recipient to provide an aid, benefit, or service under the recipient's education program or activity explicitly or impliedly conditioning the provision of such an aid, benefit, or service on a person's participation in unwelcome sexual conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classic employer/agent conditioning theory for harassment claims; focuses on authority to condition educational benefits on sexual conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostile environment harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Unwelcome sex-based conduct that, based on the totality of the circumstances, is subjectively and objectively offensive and is so severe or pervasive that it limits or denies a person's ability to participate in or benefit from the recipient's education program or activity (i.e., creates a hostile environment). Whether a hostile environment has been created is a fact-specific inquiry that includes consideration of: (i) The degree to which the conduct affected the complainant's ability to access the recipient's education program or activity; (ii) The type, frequency, and duration of the conduct; (iii) The parties' ages, roles within the recipient's education program or activity, previous interactions, and other factors about each party that may be relevant to evaluating the effects of the conduct; (iv) The location of the conduct and the context in which the conduct occurred; and (v) Other sex-based harassment in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hostile environment assessment is fact-specific and requires both subjective and objective offensiveness plus consideration of listed contextual factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific offenses (sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, stalking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific offenses include: (i) Sexual assault meaning an offense classified as a forcible or nonforcible sex offense under the FBI UCR system; (ii) Dating violence meaning violence committed by a person who is or has been in a social relationship of a romantic or intimate nature with the victim, with the existence of such a relationship determined by length, type, and frequency of interaction; (iii) Domestic violence meaning felony or misdemeanor crimes committed by a person who is a current or former spouse/intimate partner, cohabitant, shares a child in common, or commits acts against a youth/adult protected under family/domestic violence laws; or (iv) Stalking meaning engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for safety or suffer substantial emotional distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates commonly recognized criminal/abusive conduct that qualifies as sex-based harassment for Title IX purposes and provides factors for relationship determinations in dating violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note on consent definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Note 1 to the definition of sex-based harassment: The Assistant Secretary will not require a recipient to adopt a particular definition of consent, where that term is applicable with respect to sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits recipients flexibility in defining 'consent' but does not eliminate other substantive obligations in harassment definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Student means a person who has gained admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student with a disability
rubrics_metrics.description: Student with a disability means a student who is an individual with a disability as defined in the Rehabilitation Act of 1973... or a child with a disability as defined in the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links Title IX obligations to other disability statutes when students with disabilities are parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures means individualized measures offered as appropriate, as reasonably available, without unreasonably burdening a complainant or respondent, not for punitive or disciplinary reasons, and without fee or charge to the complainant or respondent to: (1) Restore or preserve that party's access to the recipient's education program or activity, including measures that are designed to protect the safety of the parties or the recipient's educational environment; or (2) Provide support during the recipient's grievance procedures under § 106.45, and if applicable § 106.46, or during the informal resolution process under § 106.44(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be individualized, non-punitive, reasonably available, and free; examples provided elsewhere in the rule include changes to housing, schedule adjustments, escorts, counseling, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Title IX Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient must designate and authorize at least one employee, referred to herein as a Title IX Coordinator, to coordinate its efforts to comply with its responsibilities under Title IX and this part. If a recipient has more than one Title IX Coordinator, it must designate one of its Title IX Coordinators to retain ultimate oversight over those responsibilities and ensure the recipient's consistent compliance with its responsibilities under Title IX and this part. As appropriate, a recipient may delegate, or permit a Title IX Coordinator to delegate, specific duties to one or more designees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires formal designation, authority, and single oversight when multiple coordinators exist; allows delegation of specific duties to designees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt, publish, and implement nondiscrimination policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient must adopt, publish, and implement a policy stating that the recipient does not discriminate on the basis of sex and prohibits sex discrimination in any education program or activity that it operates, as required by Title IX and this part, including in admission (unless subpart C does not apply) and employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nondiscrimination policies must be publicly available and cover all programs/activities the recipient operates; linked to notice and publication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must adopt, publish, and implement grievance procedures consistent with the requirements of § 106.45, and if applicable § 106.46, that provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of complaints made by students, employees, or other individuals who are participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity, or by the Title IX Coordinator, alleging any action that would be prohibited by Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures must align with the detailed procedural rules in §§ 106.45/106.46 and ensure prompt, equitable resolution for a wide set of potential complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of nondiscrimination must include: (A) A statement that the recipient does not discriminate on the basis of sex and prohibits sex discrimination in any education program or activity it operates; (B) A statement that inquiries may be referred to the Title IX Coordinator, OCR, or both; (C) The name or title, office address, email address, and telephone number of the recipient's Title IX Coordinator; (D) How to locate the recipient's nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures; and (E) How to report information about conduct that may constitute sex discrimination and how to make a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements must be included in the recipient's notice of nondiscrimination provided to listed audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice of nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient must prominently include all elements of its notice of nondiscrimination on its website and in each handbook, catalog, announcement, bulletin, and application form that it makes available to persons entitled to notice, or which are otherwise used in connection with recruitment. If necessary due to format/size, the recipient may instead include a shorter statement and provide the location of the notice on the website. A recipient must not use or distribute a publication stating that the recipient treats applicants, students, or employees differently on the basis of sex, except as such treatment is permitted by Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prominence and availability across media are required; provides a narrow exception for space-limited publications and forbids statements asserting prohibited differential treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements (general and role-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must ensure that specified persons receive training related to their duties under Title IX promptly upon hiring or change of position and annually thereafter. Training must not rely on sex stereotypes. Required trainees include: (1) All employees (trained on obligation to address sex discrimination, scope of conduct constituting sex discrimination including sex-based harassment, and applicable notification/information requirements under §§ 106.40(b)(2) and 106.44); (2) Investigators, decisionmakers, and persons implementing grievance procedures or modifying supportive measures (additional training on obligations under § 106.44; grievance procedures under § 106.45 and §106.46 if applicable; how to serve impartially and avoid prejudgment/conflicts/bias; the meaning/application of 'relevant' and impermissible evidence types); (3) Facilitators of informal resolution (trained on rules/practices and impartial service); and (4) Title IX Coordinator and designees (trained on specific responsibilities, recordkeeping, and coordination duties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies prompt and annual training, forbids reliance on sex stereotypes, and differentiates topics by role to ensure impartiality and procedural compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students with disabilities consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complainant or respondent is an elementary or secondary student with a disability, the recipient must require the Title IX Coordinator to consult with one or more members, as appropriate, of the student's IEP team or placement-decision group to determine how to comply with IDEA and Section 504 throughout implementation of grievance procedures. If a complainant or respondent is a postsecondary student with a disability, the Title IX Coordinator may consult with the designated office or individual that supports students with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires coordination between Title IX processes and disability-specific supports and legal obligations to ensure compliance with IDEA/Section 504.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping retention and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must maintain for at least seven years: (1) For each complaint of sex discrimination, records documenting the informal resolution process or the grievance procedures and the resulting outcome; (2) For each notification the Title IX Coordinator receives of information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, records documenting the actions the recipient took to meet its obligations under §106.44; and (3) All materials used to provide training under the training requirement. A recipient must make training materials available upon request for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes minimum retention period and transparency obligation for training materials; applies to complaint/investigation documentation and notice-response actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — bases of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination on the basis of sex includes discrimination on the basis of sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definition expands protected categories under 'sex' beyond traditional binary constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the part (geographic and contextual scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: This part applies to every recipient and to all sex discrimination occurring under a recipient's education program or activity in the United States. Conduct that occurs under a recipient's education program or activity includes conduct in buildings owned or controlled by a student organization officially recognized by a postsecondary institution and conduct subject to the recipient's disciplinary authority. A recipient has an obligation to address a sex-based hostile environment under its education program or activity, even when some contributing conduct occurred outside the recipient's education program or activity or outside the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that obligations can extend to conduct with connections to the recipient's program/activity even if some conduct occurs off-campus or abroad; includes student organization spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions nondiscrimination (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall, on the basis of sex, be denied admission, or be subjected to discrimination in admission, by any recipient to which this subpart applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline prohibition on sex-based discrimination in admissions for covered recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions — parental/family/marital status & pregnancy
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether a person satisfies any policy or criterion for admission, or in making any offer of admission, a recipient must treat pregnancy or related conditions in the same manner and under the same policies as any other temporary medical conditions; and must not: (i) Adopt or implement any policy, practice, or procedure concerning current/potential/past parental, family, or marital status that treats persons differently on the basis of sex; (ii) Discriminate on the basis of current/potential/past pregnancy or related conditions; or (iii) Make a pre-admission inquiry as to the marital status of an applicant (including 'Miss' or 'Mrs.'). A recipient may ask an applicant to self-identify their sex only if asked of all applicants and not used discriminatorily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits differential admissions policies based on parental or pregnancy status and forbids marriage-status pre-admission questions; treats pregnancy like other temporary medical conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education programs/activities nondiscrimination and de minimis harm test
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided elsewhere, no person shall, on the basis of sex, be excluded from participation in, be denied benefits of, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any academic, extracurricular, research, occupational training, or other education program or activity operated by a recipient. In limited circumstances where Title IX permits different treatment or separation on the basis of sex, a recipient must not carry out such treatment in a manner that discriminates by subjecting a person to more than de minimis harm; adopting a policy/practice that prevents participation consistent with a person's gender identity subjects a person to more than de minimis harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides both a broad nondiscrimination rule for programs/activities and a standard ('more than de minimis harm') for permissible sex-based separations; explicitly protects gender identity-based participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy accommodations and procedures (§ 106.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not adopt or implement any policy, practice, or procedure concerning a student's parental/family/marital status that treats students differently on the basis of sex. A recipient must not discriminate against any student based on pregnancy or related conditions and may allow voluntary separate comparable participation. The recipient must ensure Title IX Coordinator contact is provided when an employee is informed of a student's pregnancy unless the employee reasonably believes the Coordinator has been notified. The recipient must take specific actions to promptly and effectively prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access once notified; the Title IX Coordinator must coordinate these actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section contains multiple enforceable duties triggered by notification of pregnancy, including outreach, accommodations, and ensuring comparable access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — reasonable modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must make reasonable modifications to policies, practices, or procedures as necessary to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access. Each reasonable modification must be based on the student's individualized needs. A modification that the recipient can demonstrate would fundamentally alter the nature of its education program or activity is not a reasonable modification. The student has discretion to accept or decline each reasonable modification and if accepted the recipient must implement it. Examples include breaks to express breast milk, intermittent absences for medical appointments, access to online/homebound education, schedule/course sequence changes, extensions for coursework, allowing water nearby, counseling, changes in physical space or supplies, elevator access, or other changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires individualized, non-fundamentally-altering accommodations with illustrative examples; student choice in accepting modifications is explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — voluntary separate comparable participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must allow the student to voluntarily access any separate and comparable portion of the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separateness is allowed only if access is voluntary and the separate portion is comparable to mainstream offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — voluntary leave of absence
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must allow the student to voluntarily take a leave of absence from the recipient's education program or activity to cover, at minimum, the period of time deemed medically necessary by the student's licensed healthcare provider. If a recipient's leave policy allows more time than medically necessary, the recipient must permit leave under that policy if the student chooses. When the student returns, they must be reinstated to the academic status and, as practicable, extracurricular status held when the voluntary leave began.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects voluntary leave for pregnancy and requires reinstatement to prior status as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — lactation space requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must ensure that the student can access a lactation space, which must be a space other than a bathroom, that is clean, shielded from view, free from intrusion from others, and may be used by a student for expressing breast milk or breastfeeding as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies minimum characteristics for lactation spaces (not a bathroom; privacy, cleanliness, freedom from intrusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — limitation on supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not require supporting documentation for reasonable modifications, access to separate/comparable portions, voluntary leaves, lactation space, etc., unless the documentation is necessary and reasonable to determine needed modifications or further actions. Examples when documentation is not necessary include obvious needs (e.g., bigger uniform), previously provided sufficient documentation, or routine accommodations like allowing water nearby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts burdensome proof requirements; gives concrete non-exhaustive examples when documentation would be unnecessary or unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — comparable treatment to other temporary medical conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent consistent with required accommodations, a recipient must treat pregnancy or related conditions in the same manner and under the same policies as any other temporary medical conditions with respect to any medical/hospital benefit, service, plan, or policy the recipient administers, operates, offers, or participates in with respect to students admitted to the program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates parity between pregnancy-related conditions and other temporary medical conditions in institutional policies and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — certification to participate limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not require a student who is pregnant or has related conditions to provide certification from a healthcare provider or any other person that the student is physically able to participate in the class/program/extracurricular activity unless: (i) The certified level of physical ability/health is necessary for participation; (ii) The recipient requires such certification of all students participating; and (iii) The information obtained is not used as a basis for discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits pregnancy-specific fitness-for-participation certifications unless universally required and necessary for safety/participation, and forbids discriminatory use of information obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient's duty to respond promptly and effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient with knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination in its education program or activity must respond promptly and effectively; and must also comply with § 106.44 to address sex discrimination in its education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a general promptness and effectiveness standard for institutional responses to alleged sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and address barriers to reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must require its Title IX Coordinator to: (1) Monitor the recipient's education program or activity for barriers to reporting information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part; and (2) Take steps reasonably calculated to address such barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obliges proactive monitoring of reporting impediments (e.g., cultural, procedural, accessibility barriers) and taking remedial steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for employees (who must notify Title IX Coordinator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elementary/secondary recipients must require all employees who are not confidential employees to notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination. All other recipients must at minimum require: (i) Any employee who is not a confidential employee and who either has authority to institute corrective measures or responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information; and (ii) All other non-confidential employees to either notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information or provide contact information of the Title IX Coordinator and how to make a complaint to any person who provides them with such information. Postsecondaries must determine whether a person who is both a student and employee is subject to these requirements. The requirements do not apply to an employee who has personally been subject to the conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates notification duties by employee role and by elementary/secondary vs other recipients; allows some staff to act as conduits by providing contact information instead of making a report themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must notify participants how to contact any confidential employees. A confidential employee must explain to any person who informs them of conduct: (i) the employee's confidential status and circumstances where they are not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator; (ii) how to contact the Title IX Coordinator and make a complaint; and (iii) that the Title IX Coordinator may be able to offer and coordinate supportive measures and initiate informal resolution or an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets notice and intake script duties for confidential employees and requires recipients to publicize how to reach confidential resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public awareness events information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When a postsecondary institution's Title IX Coordinator is notified of information provided during a public awareness event held on campus or via an online platform sponsored by the institution, the institution is not obligated to act in response unless the information indicates an imminent and serious threat to health or safety. However, the institution must use this information to inform prevention efforts, including tailored training when information indicates possible multiple incidents. Recipients are not obligated to require attendance by Title IX staff at such events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between awareness-raising disclosures and actionable reports; mandates using event information for prevention/training but does not require investigatory action absent safety threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator response duties when notified
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, the Title IX Coordinator must take actions to promptly and effectively end any sex discrimination in the education program or activity, prevent its recurrence, and remedy its effects, including: (i) Treat the complainant and respondent equitably; (ii) Offer and coordinate supportive measures for the complainant as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions the Coordinator as the central actor to ensure equitable treatment, offer supports, coordinate remedies, and drive institutional response efforts.
